title: The ordinary DOCX edit scans the main part twice, not four times
implements: parts (a) and (b) of item DOCX-1 in the change 0587 queue (rank 4); part (c) is not implemented
reason_codes: Patch::apply reads nothing from its source snapshot but an exact byte comparison, so apply_document_patch was copying and rescanning the whole main part to answer a memcmp; the patch now answers it from main.blob() and hands back its own retained target

a same-structure direct-body paragraph rewrite determines the new layout exactly - the rewritten paragraph resizes and every later direct-body range shifts by the same delta - so the rescan it triggered rebuilt a layout that was already known
both reuses are conditional and fall back to the unchanged route, so every refusal, typed error and error identity stays where it was

the layout derivation is accepted only against a paragraph-sized proof that the replacement fragment keeps every whole-document verdict scan_document reaches: one balanced element, no more nodes, no more depth, a byte-identical root start tag

accepted_evidence.deterministic_counts: callgrind isolation pair (--samples 3 minus --samples 1, halved) on the three DOCX selectors, both legs, CPU 11: Snapshot::from_xml 12 -> 6 calls per one-edit lifecycle (280.51 M -> 140.48 M inclusive Ir) and 6 -> 3 per no-op lifecycle (140.49 M -> 70.18 M); apply_document_patch inclusive 72.91 M -> 1.66 M; whole harness iteration -19.58%, -19.34% and -16.26%
accepted_evidence.timed_region_counts: a retained probe opens a constant four packages and runs edit_document..to_stream on `measured` of them, so the same isolation pair differences two timed regions exactly: -13.96% to -33.27% on the one-edit shapes, -14.07% to -32.75% on one-percent, -43.88% to -49.73% on the no-op
accepted_evidence.paired_timing: order A1 B1 B2 A2 in one window, 100 samples per pooled leg, pinned to CPU 11: p50 -18.64% to -49.95% across all nine case/shape scenarios, with p95, p99 and mean moving the same way
accepted_evidence.floor: A/A p50 within 2.06% and B/B p50 within 1.67% in the same window, against the roughly 4% p50 this host records
accepted_evidence.differential_tests: the derived layout is compared against a full scan_document rescan on 297 accepted single rewrites across 53 DOCX fixtures (all 297 took the incremental route) and 4 batch rewrites, plus the 24/200/10,000-paragraph generated corpora at three positions and three replacement texts each, their 1% batch and their committed snapshots; the coverage counts are asserted
accepted_evidence.fallback_tests: shape-changing replacements (extra element, extra depth, different root, two roots, processing instruction, unbalanced, padded), splices off a paragraph boundary by one byte, and a declined splice producing a snapshot byte- and layout-identical to Snapshot::from_xml
accepted_evidence.patch_tests: exact no-op keeps the main part payload Arc pointer-identical; a mismatched source returns StaleSource and leaves the package untouched; the inverse still reaches the original bytes; an unparsable main part still returns TransactionError::Document rather than StaleSource
accepted_evidence.gates: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy -p litchi-docx --all-targets, cargo test -p litchi-docx (1457 passed, 0 failed, 31 ignored across 51 binaries, 9 new), cargo doc -p litchi-docx --no-deps

accepted_costs.fragment_proof: two paragraph-sized quick-xml passes per accepted rewrite: 18,126 Ir over 6 calls on the one-edit case and 620,948 Ir over 206 calls on the one-percent case, against the 140 M of scanning removed
accepted_costs.shared_host: seven other agents built and measured on the same 32-core host throughout; the A/A and B/B floors are reported as what that amounted to
accepted_costs.synthetic_corpus: the timed scenarios use the harness's generated DOCX corpora; the fixture corpus enters only through the correctness differential

known_gaps.part_c: compaction still rewrites the whole main part on every changed commit (62.5 M Ir per one-edit lifecycle) and its rescan is the second remaining scan; compacting only the replacement fragment changes output bytes for documents whose untouched paragraphs carry compactable whitespace, so it needs the owner's answer to 0587's ADR 0006 observation, then a frozen design record and preservation tests
known_gaps.other_rewrite_sites: eleven Edit call sites of with_rewritten_xml still rescan; several rewrite a paragraph inside a table or a block content control, which the derivation declines outright because it accepts only an exact direct-body paragraph range
known_gaps.document_snapshot_copy: document_snapshot still builds from main.blob().to_vec(), so the pointer half of the reuse proof never hits on the eager route and the byte comparison runs in full; handing the part's Arc to Snapshot::from_shared_xml would remove both, and is named as the next measurement rather than folded in
known_gaps.docx_2: DocumentPart::from_part still builds its paragraph index eagerly on every document() call; that is a separate 0587 item on a separate route

withheld: any registered speedup, any cold-cache, physical-device, real-producer, peak-RSS, allocation-profile, concurrency-scaling or cross-platform result, and any claim about DOCX operations other than a direct-body paragraph text rewrite and the patch application that publishes it

provenance.host: AMD EPYC 9R45, 32 cores, 123 GiB, Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws, rustc 1.95.0, valgrind 3.26.0
provenance.builds: cargo build --release --locked on both legs with identical flags; before leg from the shared read-only checkout at the base commit with its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR
